stem: A growing perpetuity pays Rs 5,000 at the end of the first year, and the payment grows at 3% per year forever. If the required annual return is 8%, what is the present value of this growing perpetuity?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Applies the simple perpetuity formula C/r = 5000/0.08 = 62,500, ignoring the growth rate g.
Divides C by (r + g) = 5000 / 0.11 = 45,455, adding the growth rate instead of subtracting it.
Divides C by (g) alone = 5000 / 0.03 = 1,66,667, using only the growth rate as the denominator.

explanation: A growing perpetuity uses the Gordon Growth Model: PV = C / (r - g), where r is the required return and g is the constant growth rate. Growth reduces the effective discount rate applied to the first payment.

explanation_sections.punchline: Gordon Growth Model PV = C / (r - g) distinguishes from C / r: growth in the denominator is subtracted, not added.
explanation_sections.lesson: The sign of g in the denominator matters critically. r - g, not r + g. If g equals r, PV is infinite (undefined).
explanation_sections.timing: 35 seconds. The trap at 62,500 ignores growth; the trap at 45,455 adds g to r in the denominator. Confirm r > g before applying the formula.
